content.overview: BNS s. 166 — Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman. BNS restatement of IPC 138. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 138. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 166 is the rule on “Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman”. The section provides that whoever abets what he knows to be an act of insubordination by an officer, soldier, sailor or airman, in the Army, Navy or Air Force, of the Government of India, shall, if such act of insubordination be committed in consequence of that abetment, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 166 exists so that “Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman” has a closed legal test in Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Mutiny, desertion, insubordination, and wearing a service garb.
